newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil, Korea joint venture to create 400 jobs.
newsitem.headline: Brazil, Korea joint venture to create 400 jobs.

text.p: A $215-million joint venture between Brazil's state mining firm CVRD and South Korea's steelmaker Posco to produce iron pellets in Brazil will create 400 jobs, a CVRD spokesman said.
Companhia do Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) and Pohang Steel and Iron Co (Posco) set up the 50-50 Kobrasco joint venture in September last year.
The CVRD spokesman said construction work on the iron pellet plant would provide 1,000 jobs, while the plant itself would create 400 direct and indirect jobs.

He said construction of the plant had not yet started, but the factory was due to take up production of 4.0 million tonnes of pellets a year in July 1998. Around 2.5 million tonnes of Kobrasco's iron pellet production will go to the South Korean market.
Kobrasco, which is located in Vitoria in the Brazilian state of Espirito Santo, is expected to have an annual turnover of $130 million.
--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
